stem: How is a π bond formed?

options.content: By sideways overlap of two parallel p orbitals.
options.rationale: Correct: the electron density lies above and below the bond axis.

options.content: By end-on overlap of two p orbitals.
options.rationale: End-on overlap gives a σ bond.

options.content: By overlap of two s orbitals.
options.rationale: s orbitals can only overlap end-on, giving a σ bond.

options.content: By overlap of two sp² hybrid orbitals.
options.rationale: Hybrid orbitals form σ bonds; π bonds use unhybridised p orbitals.

explanation: A π bond forms when two parallel p orbitals on adjacent atoms overlap sideways.

stem: How many σ bonds and π bonds are there in one molecule of ethene, C₂H₄?

options.rationale: Correct: four C–H σ, plus one σ and one π in C=C.
The C=C double bond has one σ and one π, and each C–H is a σ bond.
This counts the double bond as two σ bonds.
A double bond contains only one π bond.

explanation: C₂H₄: 4 C–H (σ) + C=C (1σ + 1π) = 5 σ and 1 π.

stem: How many σ bonds and π bonds are there in one molecule of ethanenitrile, CH₃CN?

options.rationale: A triple bond contains two π bonds.
A triple bond has only one σ and two π bonds; the C–C single bond is σ.
This counts each bond of the triple bond as a σ bond.
Correct: three C–H, one C–C and one C≡N (σ + 2π).

explanation: 3 C–H σ + C–C σ + C≡N (1σ + 2π) = 5 σ and 2 π.
hints: Draw the full structural formula: H₃C–C≡N.

stem: What is the hybridisation of each carbon atom in ethane, and what is the H–C–H bond angle?

options.rationale: sp² carbons have a double bond; ethane has only single bonds.
sp carbons are found with a triple bond or two double bonds.
Correct: four σ bonds arranged tetrahedrally.
Tetrahedral sp³ orbitals are 109.5° apart.

explanation: Each carbon in ethane forms four σ bonds using four sp³ hybrid orbitals at 109.5°.

stem: Why is there no free rotation about the C=C bond in but-2-ene?

options.content: Rotation would break the σ bond between the two carbon atoms.
options.rationale: A σ bond is symmetrical about the axis, so rotation does not affect it.

options.content: The methyl groups are too large to pass each other.
options.rationale: Bulky groups can rotate about single bonds; the restriction comes from the π bond.

options.content: Rotation would twist the p orbitals out of line and break the π bond.
options.rationale: Correct: the π overlap needs the p orbitals to stay parallel.

options.content: The two carbon atoms are sp³ hybridised.
options.rationale: The carbons of a C=C bond are sp² hybridised.

explanation: The π bond needs parallel p orbitals. Twisting one carbon relative to the other would destroy the overlap, which costs a lot of energy, so the C=C bond cannot rotate; hence cis and trans isomers.
hints: Think about what must stay parallel for sideways overlap.

stem: In propyne, CH₃–C≡CH, what are the hybridisations of the three carbon atoms, reading from left to right?

options.rationale: sp² carbons form a double bond, not a triple bond.
Correct: CH₃ has four σ bonds; each C of the triple bond has two σ bonds.
The CH₃ carbon has four single bonds, so it is sp³.
The middle carbon is part of the triple bond, so it is sp.

explanation: Four σ bonds → sp³; two σ bonds (plus two π) → sp.
hints: Count the σ bonds around each carbon.

stem:
Statements about the bonding in ethene:

1. Each carbon atom uses three sp² hybrid orbitals to form σ bonds.
2. The π bond is formed from unhybridised 2p orbitals.
3. All six atoms lie in the same plane.

Which of the statements are correct?

options.rationale: Statement 3 is true too: the sp² σ framework is planar and the p orbitals must be parallel.
Statement 1 is true: three sp² hybrids per carbon.
Statements 2 and 3 are also true.
Correct: all three are true.

explanation: Each carbon: three sp² σ bonds in a plane at 120°, one p orbital perpendicular; the two p orbitals overlap sideways (π). This forces the molecule to be planar.
hints: The p orbitals must be parallel for the π bond.

stem:
Statements about σ and π bonds:

1. A σ bond has its electron density along the axis between the nuclei.
2. A π bond is weaker than a σ bond.
3. A triple bond contains two σ bonds and one π bond.

Which of the statements are correct?

options.rationale: Statement 3 is wrong: one σ and two π.
Correct: a triple bond is one σ and two π.
Statement 1 is correct and statement 3 is wrong.
Statement 2 is also correct: sideways overlap is less effective.

explanation: σ: density on the axis; π: weaker, density above and below. Triple bond = 1σ + 2π.

stem: How many σ bonds are there in one molecule of butane, C₄H₁₀?
explanation: Ten C–H bonds plus three C–C bonds, all single (σ): 13 σ bonds.
workedSolution: 1. Ten C–H bonds plus three C–C bonds, all single (σ): 13 σ bonds.

stem: How many σ bonds are there in one molecule of benzene, C₆H₆?
explanation: Six C–C σ bonds around the ring plus six C–H σ bonds = 12. The π electrons are delocalised over the ring.
workedSolution: 1. Six C–C σ bonds around the ring plus six C–H σ bonds = 12. The π electrons are delocalised over the ring.
hints: Each carbon forms three σ bonds: two to neighbouring carbons and one to hydrogen.

stem: Propenenitrile, CH₂=CH–C≡N, is used to make acrylic fibres. How many π bonds does one molecule contain?
explanation: C=C contributes one π bond and C≡N two: 3 π bonds (and 6 σ bonds).
workedSolution: 1. C=C contributes one π bond and C≡N two: 3 π bonds (and 6 σ bonds).
hints: Count the π bonds in each multiple bond.

stem: How many σ bonds are there in one molecule of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH?
explanation: 3 C–H + C–C + C–O + O–H (all σ) + C=O (one σ, one π) = 7 σ bonds and 1 π bond.
workedSolution: 1. 3 C–H + C–C + C–O + O–H (all σ) + C=O (one σ, one π) = 7 σ bonds and 1 π bond.
hints: Bonds: three C–H, C–C, C=O, C–O and O–H.

stem: In buta-1,3-diene, CH₂=CH–CH=CH₂, all four carbon atoms are sp² hybridised.
explanation: True. Each carbon is part of a C=C bond and forms three σ bonds, so all four are sp².

stem: There is free rotation about a carbon-carbon single bond.
explanation: True. A σ bond is cylindrically symmetrical about the axis, so rotation does not reduce the overlap.

stem: Match each atom with the bonds it forms.

right.content: two σ bonds and two π bonds
one σ bond using its 1s orbital
four σ bonds and no π bond
three σ bonds and one π bond

explanation: Methane carbon: sp³, four σ. Ethene carbon: sp², three σ + one π. Ethyne carbon: sp, two σ + two π. Hydrogen: its 1s orbital overlaps end-on with a carbon hybrid orbital.

stem: Name the type of covalent bond formed by end-on overlap of orbitals.
explanation: End-on (head-on) overlap gives a σ (sigma) bond.

stem: Describe the bonding in ethene in terms of orbital overlap and hybridisation, and explain why the molecule is planar.

points.description: Each carbon is sp² hybridised: three sp² orbitals in a plane at 120°
sp² orbitals overlap end-on with H 1s orbitals and with each other to form σ bonds (C–H and C–C)
The unhybridised p orbital on each carbon overlaps sideways with the other to form a π bond (density above and below the plane)
The p orbitals must be parallel for overlap, so all six atoms lie in one plane

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each carbon atom is sp² hybridised. Its three sp² orbitals lie in a plane at 120° and overlap end-on with two hydrogen 1s orbitals and with an sp² orbital of the other carbon, forming σ bonds. Each carbon has one unhybridised 2p orbital at right angles to this plane; these two p orbitals overlap sideways to form a π bond with electron density above and below the plane. Because the p orbitals must be parallel for this overlap, both CH₂ groups are held in the same plane, so the molecule is planar.

explanation: sp² σ framework plus a p-p π bond.
hints: Start with the hybridisation, then the σ framework, then the π bond.

stem: Explain why the bond energy of a C≡C bond is less than three times that of a C–C bond.

points.description: A C≡C bond is one σ bond plus two π bonds
π bonds are weaker than σ bonds because sideways overlap is less effective than end-on overlap

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The triple bond is one σ bond and two π bonds. Sideways overlap of p orbitals is less effective than end-on overlap, so each π bond is weaker than a σ bond and the total is less than three times the single bond.

explanation: π bonds are weaker than σ bonds.
hints: What are the second and third bonds in a triple bond?

stem: Describe the bonding in the nitrogen molecule, N₂, in terms of σ and π bonds formed from p orbitals.

points.description: One σ bond from end-on overlap of a 2p orbital on each N (along the bond axis)
Two π bonds from sideways overlap of the remaining pairs of parallel 2p orbitals
The two π bonds are at right angles to each other (each nitrogen keeps a lone pair)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each nitrogen atom has three half-filled 2p orbitals. One pair of 2p orbitals pointing along the axis overlaps end-on to give the σ bond. The other two pairs overlap sideways to give two π bonds, in planes at right angles to each other. Each nitrogen keeps its 2s lone pair.

explanation: N≡N = 1σ + 2π, the π bonds perpendicular.
